title: Using Innovative Machine Learning to Detect Organized Support and Opposition to E-cigarette Use Prevention Campaign Messaging on Twitter and TikTok
text: Social media have been increasingly used to disseminate e-cigarette use prevention messages, however, very limited research has comprehensively examined the amount, themes, and sources of these campaigns and the social networks embedded in the campaign conversations. This project will fill this gap by measuring reach and engagement of such campaigns and analyzing comparative themes, major strategies countering these interventions, and the social networks upon which campaign effectiveness depends. These insights will then be used to develop concepts and technologies to help create effective social media campaigns preventing e-cigarette use among youth and young adults.

title: Predoctoral Training Program in Molecular Pharmacology
text:
For over three decades the PhD training program in Molecular Pharmacology and Experimental Therapeutics
(MPET) in the Mayo Clinic Graduate School of Biomedical Sciences (MCGSBS) has been training outstanding
researchers with the interdisciplinary background and skills to make exciting basic research discoveries and
then propel these discoveries toward novel therapies for human diseases. We are requesting funding to
support a program with a track record of producing outstanding scientists.

title: AI enhanced lifetime-based mesoscopic in vivo imaging of tissue molecular heterogeneity
text:
A novel analytic preclinical longitudinal molecular imaging platform that can dissect and quantify intratumor
heterogeneity at high-resolution in the context of targeted drug delivery will be developed. Fusion of lifetime-
sensing and high-density fluorescence intensity imaging in the Short-Wave Infrared window will provide near
cellular resolution maps of subcutaneous xenograft tumors and patient derived xenograft models. Vasculature
and glucose metabolism datasets will be integrated with distribution of target engagement of well-known
therapeutic antibodies to quantify intratumor heterogeneity at high-resolution in live, intact animals.

title: Developing a smartphone-based intervention targeting high-risk situations of nicotine vaping among young adults
text:
Interventions to reduce e-cigarette use (nicotine vaping) among young adults is urgently needed given high
prevalence of vaping in this age group, emerging vaping-related harms, and increased risk of tobacco smoking
and other substance use escalation. This study innovatively capitalizes on cutting-edge methods of mobile health
research to develop and pilot test a smartphone-based intervention delivering messages tailored to risky
moments for vaping occurrence. This study will lay the groundwork for evidence-based innovative interventions
to curb the vaping epidemic and prevent related harms among young people.

title: Effects of cannabis use on community-based alcohol treatment outcomes in adolescents
text:
Most adolescents in treatment for alcohol use disorder and co-occurring disorders (AUD+CODs) use cannabis,
yet little is known about the impact cannabis use has on AUD+COD treatment processes and outcomes.
Consistent with NIAAA’s strategic plan to improve AUD+COD treatment, this K23 will use mixed methods to
prioritize and understand adolescents’ experiences using cannabis in the context of community-based
treatment for AUD+CODs, elucidate the dynamic effects of cannabis on treatment processes as they unfold
when adolescents are using cannabis in their natural environments, and provide preliminary data on cannabis-
related predictors of longer-term AUD+COD treatment outcomes. Results will inform productive and
meaningful cannabis-related targets for AUD+COD treatment and inform models of addressing polysubstance
use in treatment.

title: Communication Optimization via Artificial Intelligence for Dentistry (CoAID):  Validating a Three-Stage Digital Health Platform to Enhance Dental Care  Communication
text:
Ineffective dentist-patient communication drives non-adherence, worsening preventable oral health disparities
and costing $45.9 billion annually.1 CoAID, an AI-driven module within Intellident’s cloud-based platform, opti-
mizes communication through personalized scripts tailored to patient needs, real-time AI analysis of interactions,
and predictive follow-ups in patients’ preferred languages. Building on a small-scale pilot showing 80% accuracy
in summarizing visit discussions and improved clarity (4/5 dentists), this STTR Phase I project will focus on vali-
dating the usability, workflow integration, and technical accuracy of CoAID in the specific context of oral surgery
and dental implant care — where communication breakdowns are particularly consequential.
This project directly supports NIDCR’s strategic priority of developing, testing, and implementing new digital health
technologies. By focusing on CoAID’s integration into everyday dental workflows and demonstrating its feasibility
in a high-impact use case, we will lay the groundwork for broader adoption of AI-driven communication tools that
advance patient-centered care.

title: A multi-level framework for characterizing task-efficient coding geometry of neural population activities
text: Rapid progress in experimental neuroscience techniques and machine learning-based models for the brain presents a common challenge in understanding high-dimensional (many neurons) neural representations in an interpretable and quantifiable way. This proposal represents a path to a multi-level framework for connecting neural representational geometry to multiple scales (neurons to regions) and levels of computational abstraction, such as (i) the effect of single neuron tuning properties on neural representations, (ii) the role of region-to-region transformations and task-learning, and (iii) new algorithms for training neural network models of the brain via geometry and machine learning. The synergy between two modern approaches – task-efficient representational geometry and machine learning – will lead to new fundamental principles and methods in computational neuroscience and enable multi-level, multi-scale theory of neural representations and discover common principles of neural computation across different brain regions and multiple modalities.

title: Assessment of microvascular volume in smokers using AI
text:
Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a heterogeneous high mortality lung condition, characterized
by airflow obstructions and pulmonary vascular endothelial damage. In the research outlined in the following
proposal, we aim to define and evaluate quantitative markers of pulmonary microvasculature injury using non-
contrast CT scans and investigate correlations with emphysema development and progression. The results of
this work will enhance our understanding of the principal mechanisms underlying pulmonary vascular damage
and extend our knowledge of their role in the etiology and progression of COPD and emphysema.

title: Spatial Frequency Domain Imaging to Investigate Mechanistic Constituents in Active Thyroid Eye Disease
text:
Thyroid eye disease affects approximately 0.1% of the United States population, yet there is currently no
standardized approach for diagnosis, longitudinal monitoring, and therapeutic decision-making in this condition.
This project utilizes spatial frequency domain imaging to examine tissue volumes within the periocular region of
patients with thyroid eye disease to establish objective and continuous optical biomarkers of disease activity.
These findings will provide valuable insights for developing metrics to assess therapeutic response, and
potentially uncover novel therapeutic targets for inflammatory oculofacial disease.

title: Knowledge-Guided Multi-Omics Integration and Transfer Learning for Emerging Infections
text:
Melioidosis is a severe bacterial infectious disease that causes high mortality but remains neglected due to
limited diagnostic and prognostic tools. This project seeks to develop knowledge-guided machine learning
approaches, including penalized neural networks and transfer learning, to integrate multi-omics and clinical
data, uncover disease mechanisms and improve prediction of patient outcomes. The findings will generate new
biological insights and advance the development of better diagnostic and prognostic strategies for melioidosis
and other emerging infectious diseases.

title: Developing cross-platform fluorescent reporters for measuring the 26S proteasome and the VCP activities
text:
A hallmark of aging is the loss of proteostasis that is caused by a progressive decline of the activity of the protein
degradation system. Studies of aging and age-related diseases often require measuring the activities of the 26S
proteasome and the VCP/p97, which are the two master regulators in the eukaryotic protein degradation system.
In the proposed study, we aim to develop a suite of cross-platform fluorescent reporters to effectively measure
the activities of the 26S proteasome and the VCP both in vitro and in vivo and validate their performance in
mouse and patient samples that are commonly involved in studies of aging and neurodegenerative diseases,
such as Alzheimer’s Disease and Related Dementias.

title: Targeting Menin in Acute Leukemia with Upregulated HOX Genes
text:
We are proposing to develop the next generation of small molecule inhibitors of the menin-MLL1 interaction and
assess their activity in advanced models of leukemia with upregulated HOX genes. Ultimately, such compounds
are expected to become highly specific drugs for patients with aggressive forms of acute leukemia, which poorly
respond to current therapies.

title: Molecular mechanisms underlying alcohol-induced congenital heart defects
text:
The long-term goal of this research is to identify molecular, cellular, and genetic mechanisms underlying
congenital heart defects and adult cardiac dysfunction in individuals with fetal alcohol spectrum disorders
(FASDs). We propose to accomplish this goal through a comprehensive evaluation of cardiomyocyte and anterior
endoderm cell populations in a zebrafish model embryonic alcohol exposure through mutant line
characterization, time-lapse imaging, single cell RNA-sequencing and spatial transcriptomics. Our findings will
expand our mechanistic understanding of the effects of prenatal alcohol exposure on the heart and reveal genetic
susceptibility loci or biomarkers that could enable the early identification of FASD patients who are at risk for
cardiovascular disease.

title: 3D In vivo dosimetry for FLASH proton therapy
text:
The field of FLASH radiotherapy has experienced wide interest and growth and could be a critical area of
development for better normal tissue sparing in radiotherapy. The Overall Objective of this application is to use
protoacoustic/ultrasound imaging to precisely guide FLASH proton therapy which will greatly facilitate the
investigation, translation, and adoption of FLASH therapy to benefit cancer patients by reducing the toxicities of
radiation therapy on cancer patient.

title: CORE 1: Data Management and Bioinformatics Core
text: DATA MANAGEMENT AND BIOINFORMATICS CORE SUMMARY The HPMI Data Management and Bioinformatics Core will support the Center's mission in all stages of research and publication, facilitating reproducible analysis, visualization, and access to center data and results. The Core will be composed of four major components: software and analysis workflows for data integration the Cytoscape and the Cytoscape Ecosystem; the Network Data Exchange (NDEx); and the HPMI Data and Analysis Portal. First, we will develop workflows to integrate proteomics, transcriptomics, genetics, and functional data generated by Projects 1 and 2 with existing -omics and GWAS datasets to select host factor candidates for validation. Second, Cytoscape will provide a range of tools for analyzing and visualizing molecular networks, interaction data, and hierarchical network models from both Projects. The third component, NDEx, will provide database infrastructure to support the sharing, reviewing, and disseminating of network data and models. It will also enable consolidated access to public biological network resources for use by HPMI investigators. Finally, the HPMI Data and Analysis Portal will provide a common access point for software tools and pipelines and their associated data. The above components – software and analysis workflows for data integration, visual network maps in Cytoscape, and storage of networks and models in NDEx – will all be made accessible through the HPMI’s website. Additionally, publications using HPMI products will be enhanced by the recent additions to Cytoscape for dynamically embedding network data in peer- reviewed journals. Finally, the Core will draw on an impressive array of hardware infrastructure for supercomputing, including high performance clusters at multiple sites.

title: Functional tests of non-coding DNA variants associated with risk for orofacial cleft
text:
Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) and linkage studies have identified common DNA
variants that are associated with elevated risk for isolated oral facial cleft, a common birth
defect. However, common variation does not explain all of the heritable risk for clefts. Moreover,
it is unclear which common variants are actually pathogenic, by what mechanism they are
pathogenic, and whether they are sufficient to increase the penetrance of cleft in an animal
model. We address these questions with analysis of whole genome sequence data to find de
novo non-coding variants, with functional tests of candidate SNPs with in cell lines and induced
pluripotent stem cells, and by engineering risk genotypes of functional SNPs into cleft-prone
mouse strains.

title: Multi-scale analysis of Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG) resistant tumor micro-environment in non-muscle invasive bladder cancer to identify novel therapeutic axis
text:
Intravesical Mycobacterium bovis Bacillus Calmette–Guérin (BCG) is the only US Food and
Drug Administration (FDA)-approved first-line treatment option for high-risk Non-muscle invasive bladder
cancer (NMIBC), and yet ~55% of patients experience the therapy resistance. Through generating molecular
atlas of single-nuclei RNA & ATAC sequencing, near-cell resolution spatial transcriptome, and bulk RNA
sequencing on retrospective cohort of pre- and post-BCG patients, we will generate multi-scale molecular
network models integrating multi-omics data at cellular resolutions. These will generate de novo BCG
resistance mechanisms, regulators and identify drugs to abolish the BCG resistance axis to shed light on the
currently unmet clinical needs.

title: Cancer Prevention through Geospatial and Temporal Examination of Environmental Effects on Smoking and Quitting
text:
Under parent grant R01CA229305, our innovative research program integrated mobile-phone based location
tracking and ecological momentary assessment (EMA) to demonstrate that repeated, real-world exposure to
tobacco retailers predicts increases in cigarette craving and smoking, thereby increasing cancer risk. The next
critical step for cancer control is to expand our novel analytic framework for understanding how risk factors in
people's daily environments affect their craving and smoking behavior, both when smoking as usual and during
an abstinence attempt. Successful completion of these aims will create public resources, expand our analytical
framework for targeting environmental situation management, and lay the foundation for dramatic advances in
tobacco control.

title: Dominantly Inherited Alzheimer Network Biomarker Core
text: Core E: Biomarker PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT There is a need to further develop classic biomarkers along with the proposal of new ones for Alzheimer disease (AD) diagnostic and progression, especially due to the recent approval of two disease modifying therapies. The Dominantly Inherited Alzheimer Network (DIAN) poses a unique opportunity to model the natural history of the asymptomatic phases of the disease, due to the known estimated age of onset of the participants. DIAN has already yielded important insights on cut-off values, the estimated biomarker trajectories, and timing for fluid biomarkers. CSF biomarkers are regularly used to aid in diagnosis of AD using the amyloid/tau/neurodegeneration (ATN) criteria. All these measures are available for all DIAN samples; thus, we propose continuation of CSF measurements to increase the scientific knowledge on their biological meaning. CSF and imaging biomarkers have proven helpful in the detection of AD; however, they are invasive, expensive, not scalable, and difficult to implement in areas that are remote or have limited resources. Recent breakthroughs in blood-based biomarkers have begun to address these limitations. The DIAN Fluid Biomarker Core (Core E) has actively participated in the identification and measurement of the proposed biomarkers and will incorporate established plasma measures as part of its standard procedures. Core E will also perform a review on all the CSF biomarker data collected during the last 15 years to evaluate: (i) overall quality, and (ii) genetic modulators of biomarker trajectory (family specific and gene specific). To increase the number of measurements available, Core E will also leverage the NulisaSeq 120 CNS panel in CSF and plasma to explore the role of neurodegeneration in Autosomal Dominant AD and high-resolution mass spectrometry.

title: Mechanisms of Psilocybin-Induced Restoration of Cognitive Flexibility Following Chronic Stress
text:
Cognitive flexibility is impaired in a wide variety of stress-related disorders, including Major
Depressive Disorder (MDD). Psychedelic-assisted therapy has shown promising early results in reducing
depressive symptoms and improving cognitive flexibility in patients with MDD. This project aims to investigate
the basic behavioral, receptor, and neural mechanisms through which psychedelics affect cognitive flexibility
following chronic stress.
